reason: The paper rider can show whether the cord itself travels along with the wiggle.
expectation: The rider will reveal how the cord moves as the wave passes.

effect: The rider showed that the disturbance travels while the cord moves locally, so I can now explore how adjusting the cord changes its motion.
reaction: The distinction between the travelling wave and the bobbing rider is satisfying.
reason: The tension-adjusting key looks suited to changing how the wave behaves on the cord.

choice.with: Wave cord with a paper rider

expectation: Adjusting the tension will change the visible wave.

effect: Adjusting tension and speed revealed a standing pattern with two loops and a nearly still point. I can now prepare the cord to be played as a string.
reaction: The stationary loops are an interesting contrast to the travelling wiggle.
reason: The movable bridge should prepare the cord for playing like a string.
expectation: The bridge will create a playable length of cord.

effect: The bridge establishes a changeable vibrating length and transfers vibration to the soundbox, preparing the cord to be played.
reaction: The connection between the bridge and soundbox is interesting.
reason: The soft plectrum is the natural tool for plucking the prepared cord.

choice.with: Cord resting on a movable bridge

expectation: Plucking the cord will make it vibrate and produce a sound.

effect: Plucking confirmed that the soundbox makes the vibration easier to hear and that shortening the vibrating cord raises the note. The machine can also return to its wave demonstration.
reaction: The change in pitch was a satisfying connection between the visible waves and sound.

mostWorthwhile.text: Plucking the cord and moving the bridge was most worthwhile: it connected a physical change in vibrating length to an audible change in pitch.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the bridge was useful, but as an action it felt more like straightforward preparation than a discovery on its own.

surprise.text: The rider stayed near its own place while the disturbance travelled along the cord; the two stationary loops were another unexpected contrast.

arbitrary.text: None of the actions felt particularly arbitrary; each piece had a clear purpose in observing or playing the cord.

continue.text: Yes. The short experiments made wave motion and pitch tangible, and I would be curious to see what the fair builds next.
